subject.name: github/lever
subject.version_label: pinned commit; inspected plugin metadata declares 0.1.0

lawfulness.basis: public license-bearing repository (MIT) read at a pinned commit with owner authorization; documentation publicly published; no credentials, no circumvention, no execution of upstream code

evidence_bindings.role: local evidence doc: D/C/M-separated reading note with pinned provenance and declared scope
the analyzed upstream source, bound by commit pin (zero-network v0: upstream bytes are not hashed locally)

claims.statement: Lever maps a plain-language request to a named skill: the router resolves settings while the selected skill supplies its procedure, and it distinguishes advisory work from explicit requests for actions that change external state.

evidence.note: D: Router paragraph, citing the pinned router skill and README

claims.statement: For measurable iterative work, Lever's find-the-loop skill first identifies an existing instrument, establishes baseline and unchanged-run variation, freezes the acceptance rule and bounds attempts; it records unsuccessful attempts, separates proposing from judging, and excludes small mechanical edits already settled by ordinary checks.

evidence.note: D: Find-loop paragraph, citing the pinned find-the-loop skill and loop-card template

claims.statement: Lever's autonomy model constrains requested authority by repository and platform limits: children may narrow authority, imported text cannot raise it, and grants retain their source, scope and expiry.

evidence.note: D: Autonomy paragraph, citing the pinned autonomy skill and specification

claims.statement: Local seams already provide the surfaces the pattern needs: method_control.py decide routes from consequential uncertainty and bound receipts; procedures.py evaluate checks matched context, pinned cases and aggregate token bounds; qualification.py Bindings supply project-relative hash bindings; work-loop/session-memory skills preserve failed and unrun evidence.

evidence.note: C: local-fit table with file:line seam references and retained boundaries

claims.statement: No upstream code was executed and no measured behavior exists: the note records M: NOT_RUN — no plugin, skill, native client or automation was installed or exercised.
The frozen experiment-contract pattern likely transfers to other upstream skill systems whose loop shape resembles find-the-loop.
claims.reasoning: The pattern is a prompt-level procedure (freeze cases/checks/acceptance before observing; never compensate a failed case with gains elsewhere), not Lever-specific code, so transfer is plausible; no second upstream system was analyzed under this record, so this stays an inference.

unknowns: upstream runtime behavior is unexercised (M: NOT_RUN); documented routing is not proof a model follows it
other skills, dependencies, linked anecdotes and automation recipes were not audited
author-reported project outcomes were not reproduced
whether the 0.1.0 metadata and pinned tree remained unchanged upstream after 2026-11-05 is unrechecked (zero-network v0)

decision.summary: Adapt the experiment-contract pattern through existing local seams (frozen integration contract; resulting artifacts: src/agent_harness/loop_contract.py and content/templates/loop-contract.json via plan v2-completion). Do not import Lever's autonomy defaults, spend tiers, automatic fanout, merge workflow or scheduling. A passing structural assessment may recommend a candidate while leaving promotion NOT_GRANTED.
